rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE REVISED PHILIPPINE MEDICAL CARE ACT (P.D. NO. 1519) SO AS TO INCLUDE INDIGENTS, AS CERTIFIED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, IN THE COVERAGE OF MEDICAL CARE BENEFITS
rows.abstract: Defines "INDIGENT" as a person certified by the DSWD as needy and poor, or one who has not sufficient property to furnish a living nor anyone able to support him to whom he is entitled to look for support. Proposes the following --- "SEC. 15 ENTITLEMENT TO MEDICAL CARE BENEFITS, A MEMBER WHO SHALL HAVE PAID AT LEAST THREE MONTHLY CONTRIBUTIONS DURING THE LAST TWELVE MONTHS PRIOR TO THE FIRST DAY OF THE SINGLE PERIOD OF CONFINEMENT, AS WELL AS HIS LEGAL DEPENDENTS, SHALL BE ENTITLED TO MEDICAL CARE BENEFITS: PROVIDED, THAT WHEN WE COMMITS ANY VIOLATION OF THIS LAW OR ITS RULES AND REGULATIONS, HE AND HIS LEGAL DEPENDENTS SHALL NOT BE ALLOWED TO AVAIL OF THESE BENEFITS BY THE COMMISSION SUBJECT TO SECTON 6(K) HEREOF.  THE MEMBER SHALL CONTINNUE TO PAY HIS CONTRIBUTION DURING THE PERIOD OF SUSPENSION OF AVAILMENT OF BENEFITS: PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT AN INDIGENT AS DEFINED HEREIN, SHALL BE ENTITLED TO THE BENEFITS PROVIDED FOR IN THIS ACT."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1996-02-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ADOPT A REVISED GOVERNMENT AUDITING CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES REVISING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1445, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'THE GOVERNMENT AUDITING CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES'
rows.abstract: "Government Auditing Code of 1995" Aims to --- (1) Remove statutory hindrances to the complete implementation of an engagement or team approach audit; (2) Disengage COA from non-audit functions to enable it to concentrate more on revenue, performance and fraud audits; (3) Provide COA Auditors access to vital documents in the custody of government agencies deemed necessary for audit purposes; (4) Grant to COA the authority to restructure its organization and functions; (5) Enhance accountabilityof public funds and property of goernment officers; (6) Impose penal sanctions for obstructing COA's audit and exercise of jurisdiction; (7) Operationalize the collegial concept of COA leadership unde the Constitution; and (8) Amend requirements orprovisions which are mere procedural detail impractical, unreasonable, or outmoded.

rows.abstract: Is base on the observation that with the increasing internationaliz ation of commerce in the world today, it is inevitable that the filing of lawsuits between persons of different nationalities is also on the rise. rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A NATIONAL ALCOHOLISM REHABILITATION CENTER IN LUZON, VISAYAS, AND MINDANAO, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Prescribes the following functions of the proposed NATIONAL ALCOHOLISM REHABILITATION CENTER: (1) Educate the people on the nature of alcoholism as a disease and how it can be treated; (2) Encourage alcoholics to undergo treatment in rehabilitationcenters; (3) Help lessen the number of crimes being committed in the country under the influence of alcohol; (4) Provide alcoholics with government subsidized health care services relating to the treatment of alcoholism; (5) Draw up, in consultationwith various agencies, a national treatment and rehabilitation program for alcoholics; and (6) Grant technical or financial assitance to other rehabilitation centers for alcholics under guidelines to be approved by the Department of Health.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1996-02-13
